subcategory: legal: hierarchical legal graph + Researcher-Auditor-Adjudicator multi-agent GraphRAG
task: Legal judgment prediction (charge, article, term of penalty)
problem: Flat GraphRAG cannot separate facts, rules and principles in heterogeneous legal corpora, and retrieve-then-generate pipelines pass unverified, noisy context to the LLM; adding 6 irrelevant documents drops charge accuracy from 42.8 to 29.8.
architecture: LegalGraphRAG: HierarGraph organises legal sources into fact, rule and ontology graphs; a Researcher agent retrieves candidate cases and articles, an Auditor verifies each article against case facts using diagnostic checklists and judicial interpretations, and an Adjudicator synthesises the verified evidence into a cited judgment.
retriever: graph retrieval over HierarGraph with BGE-m3 embeddings
knowledge_source: Chinese criminal case datasets, statutes and judicial interpretations
key_results: Average accuracy over CAIL and CMDL sub-fields 49.5 vs 43.1 for RAPTOR and HippoRAG2, 42.8 for DeepSeek-V3.1 and 33.3 for Naive RAG (Qwen3-8B backbone).
On CMDL Public Safety: 65.5 ACC / 66.5 F1 vs 53.8 / 62.6 for RAPTOR.
strengths: Explicit verification step against statutes yields citable, transparent reasoning chains.
Broad baselines spanning general LLMs, legal LLMs and graph-RAG methods.

limitations.text: Limited to textual inputs; non-textual evidence (photos, video, audio) must be transcribed, losing nuance.
Historical judgment data may carry regional or gender biases.
Only Chinese criminal law benchmarks are evaluated.

title: LegalGraphRAG: Multi-Agent Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Reliable Legal Reasoning
